page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highmem-112 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 112 dedicated vCPUs derived from 56 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2.0 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 896 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate top-tier capabilities in multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test places this instance in the top 10% with a score of 164204.56, complemented by a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 94622.94. Memory performance is highly competitive, with cached read-only small block bandwidth reaching 7672.69 GB/sec and large block write bandwidth at 136.46 GB/sec. The system also excels in cryptographic execution, scoring in the top 10% on the PassMark CPU encryption test, and shows strong capabilities in ray tracing and software compilation.

From a resource density perspective, the c2d-highmem-112 offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the overhead of GPU hardware. However, a notable tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring external network-attached storage solutions. While the instance demonstrates strong performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, its text generation speeds for larger LLM models are weak, as shown by a 2.75 tokens/sec rate on a 70B model. This server is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, memory-intensive data processing, software compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
